# Skales

> Websites & systems for service businesses. Builds websites, online booking and follow-up automation for UK service businesses (trades and local operators). Run by Tom Griffiths, one person, in the United Kingdom.

Key facts:
- Builds websites, online booking and follow-up automation for UK service businesses (trades and local operators).
- One person: the person you message is the person who builds it.
- Twelve websites and one system run live on the site as working demonstrations; every business in them is fictional.
- One system a week is built in public on Instagram.
- Clients own their domain, code and accounts from day one; nothing is rented back to them monthly.
- Every build is hand-coded, with no page builder and no theme.
- Contact: thomasrgriffiths08@gmail.com · Instagram @tomxsystems (https://www.instagram.com/tomxsystems/)
- Book a call: https://skales.studio/book/

## Pages
- [Home](https://skales.studio/): what Skales builds, with a live demonstration build on the page.
- [Work: twelve websites and one system](https://skales.studio/work/): every demonstration website and every part of the system, each running live and each with its own page.
- [Websites](https://skales.studio/work/websites/): the four kinds of website (loud, motion, quiet, direct) with every example.
- [The system](https://skales.studio/work/system/): the one app behind the websites, as an overview screen plus six parts (inbox and missed calls, booking, quotes, reviews, reminders, results), shown for six made-up businesses.
- [Services](https://skales.studio/services/): the five services, built as one system: [Websites](https://skales.studio/services/websites/), [Booking and CRM](https://skales.studio/services/booking-and-crm/), [Follow-up automation](https://skales.studio/services/follow-up-automation/), [Meta ads](https://skales.studio/services/meta-ads/), [Google ads](https://skales.studio/services/google-ads/).
- [Automations](https://skales.studio/automations/): [missed-call text-back](https://skales.studio/automations/missed-call-text-back/), [review requests](https://skales.studio/automations/review-requests/), [service reminders](https://skales.studio/automations/service-reminders/), [quote chasing](https://skales.studio/automations/quote-chasing/), [booking deposits](https://skales.studio/automations/booking-deposits/), [on-my-way texts](https://skales.studio/automations/on-my-way-texts/).
- [Try it](https://skales.studio/try/): live demos that run in the browser: a missed call texted back and booked, online booking with a deposit, and a CRM board whose follow-up texts send themselves.
- [Compare](https://skales.studio/compare/): honest comparisons against [a page builder](https://skales.studio/compare/page-builders/), [a monthly trade website](https://skales.studio/compare/trade-website-templates/), [a missed-call app](https://skales.studio/compare/missed-call-apps/), [a directory listing](https://skales.studio/compare/directories/), [a Google Business Profile alone](https://skales.studio/compare/google-business-profile/), [a Facebook page](https://skales.studio/compare/facebook-page/).

## The builds
- [Atelier Voss](https://skales.studio/work/atelier-voss/): website for an invented architecture practice: An architecture practice whose four projects sit beside the drawings that made them.
- [Cadence](https://skales.studio/work/cadence/): website for an invented software company: A product page where the board runs a real shift while you watch.
- [Marée](https://skales.studio/work/maree/): website for an invented fragrance house: A real bottle on a black stage, ink in the water, and a clock for the notes.
- [SIGNAL 2027](https://skales.studio/work/signal/): website for an invented festival: A real crowd, a poster you can tap, and tickets with the fee shown up front.
- [Long Exposure](https://skales.studio/work/long-exposure/): website for an invented film production company: A film company whose first screen is its showreel, with the timecode and scrub bar on top.
- [Overhead](https://skales.studio/work/overhead/): website for an invented drone survey & filming: A drone survey firm whose survey lines draw themselves over real aerial photos as you scroll.
- [Southpaw](https://skales.studio/work/southpaw/): website for an invented boxing club: A boxing club site run by a live round timer, with the week straight under it.
- [Marrow & Pin](https://skales.studio/work/marrow-and-pin/): website for an invented tattoo studio: A tattoo studio whose flash wall inks itself, stencil to black, as you scroll.
- [Hale & Partners](https://skales.studio/work/hale-and-partners/): website for an invented accountant: An accountant's site that counts down to your next deadline from the first screen.
- [Fern Physio](https://skales.studio/work/fern-physio/): website for an invented physiotherapy clinic: A drawn body with ten tappable points, and a booking flow behind it.
- [Kestrel Electrical](https://skales.studio/work/kestrel-electrical/): website for an invented electrician: An electrician's page built as a fuse board: every job is a breaker.
- [Kerb & Camber](https://skales.studio/work/kerb-and-camber/): website for an invented garage: A UK number plate you type into, and the MOT date that comes back.
- [The system](https://skales.studio/work/system/): part of the system, shown for six invented businesses: One screen: every call caught, every job booked, and what still needs you.
- [Inbox and missed calls](https://skales.studio/work/inbox/): part of the system, shown for six invented businesses: Every call, text and form in one list. Missed calls get a text back in seconds.
- [Booking and the diary](https://skales.studio/work/booking/): part of the system, shown for six invented businesses: Customers book a real free time and pay a deposit. It lands in the right diary.
- [Quotes that chase themselves](https://skales.studio/work/quotes/): part of the system, shown for six invented businesses: Quotes from your price list that chase themselves until the customer answers.
- [Google reviews](https://skales.studio/work/reviews/): part of the system, shown for six invented businesses: Every finished job asks for a review. Replies take one tap.
- [Reminders that rebook](https://skales.studio/work/reminders/): part of the system, shown for six invented businesses: Yearly services, MOTs and regular cuts remind the customer and book themselves.
- [Results and ads](https://skales.studio/work/results/): part of the system, shown for six invented businesses: Where every job came from, what it was worth, and what the ads cost per job.

## Frequently asked
- **Do I actually own the website?** Yes. With Skales the domain, the code and the hosting sit in your own accounts from day one. It is set up so you could walk away tomorrow and lose nothing; that is the whole point.
- **Is there a monthly fee to keep my site online?** No. Skales does not charge a monthly platform fee to keep your own website alive. You pay for hosting and your domain directly, in your own name, at cost. If any quote you get includes a monthly fee to keep your own site online, that is rent.
- **How long does a build take?** A website on its own takes days. A full system with booking and follow-up usually takes one to two weeks. You get a date with the quote, and you can watch it being built in public.
- **Are the builds on this site real clients?** No, and deliberately so. Every business, person, review and phone number in the demonstration builds is invented, so nothing on this site exposes anyone Skales works with. They are real working software, just for businesses that do not exist.
- **Who actually does the work?** Tom Griffiths. Skales is one person: there is no account manager and no handover to a junior. The person you message is the person who builds it.
- **What kind of businesses is this for?** UK service businesses whose work comes in by phone: plumbers, heating engineers, electricians, roofers, kitchen fitters, landscapers, cleaners, salons and similar trades and local operators.
- **What happens after I book a call or send the form?** Tom Griffiths looks at your website, your Google listing and what happens when someone tries to reach you, then messages you three things: what is leaking, what to fix first, and what it is worth in jobs. If you want it fixed, you get a flat quote. If not, you keep the list.
- **Do you use page-builders or templates?** No. Every build is hand-coded, with no page builder and no theme, so it does exactly what your business needs and nothing it does not.

### Four kinds of website. (https://skales.studio/work/websites/)

Website examples for service businesses | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Work / Websites Four kinds of website. A boxing club and an accountant should not get the same site. The first decision is the lane: how loud, how much moves, how fast it gets to the phone number. Every example is a full website for an invented business, running live. Loud Big, bold, confident. The type is the image and one moment does the talking. 3 examples · Gyms, bars, studios, events: anyone who needs to be noticed before they are compared. Motion The page is the film: a showreel first screen, scroll-driven sequences, timecodes. 3 examples · Film, video, drone and photography businesses: anyone selling moving pictures. Quiet Plain, calm, expensive. Almost nothing moves; the typography does the work. 3 examples · Accountants, clinics, architects, solicitors: businesses whose customers are buying reassurance. Direct Conversion first. One-tap call, a three-field form, the service area, no fluff. 3 examples · Trades and local services that live off the phone. When does a business need a loud website? When being remembered matters more than being reassured. A boxing club or a tattoo studio is chosen on feel, so the site moves, the type hits and there is one thing the visitor will describe to a friend. Everything still works: the number, the booking and the address are one tap away. SIGNAL 2027 A real crowd, a poster you can tap, and tickets with the fee shown up front. Like a film. The work plays on the first screen, the visitor scrubs through it by scrolling, and the page carries a timecode. Footage is sized for phones so it starts fast, and the story reads even if you never scroll. Marée A real bottle on a black stage, ink in the water, and a clock for the notes. Website · Drone survey & filming Why would a business choose a plain website? Because its customers are buying trust, not excitement. A quiet page uses real typography, generous space and one accent, and moves exactly once. It is harder to make than a loud one, because nothing is hiding behind an animation. Atelier Voss is a working website built for an invented architecture practice. An architect sells the drawing and the building. This site shows both, side by side, and links them point by point. What is in it The name huge over a full-screen photo of a finished building Four projects, each a photo beside its drawing sheet Plans, sections and elevations that draw themselves as you scroll Numbered callouts linking each drawing to the same spot in the photo An enquiry form laid out as the practice's own title block Real buildings beside their drawings Drawings that draw as you scroll An enquiry on a title block How it was built By hand, with nothing bought in Written By hand, as a single self-contained page. ### Websites, booking, follow-up and ads (https://skales.studio/services/)

Websites, booking, follow-up and ads | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Services Websites, booking, follow-up and ads for service businesses. Skales builds five things for UK trades and service businesses: a website that turns a visit into a job, online booking with a CRM, follow-up texts that send themselves, and Meta and Google ads that point at all three. They work as one system, and everything is set up in your name. Book a call Try the live demos 01 Websites A fast site built to turn a visit into a call, a booking or an enquiry you can ring back. More → 02 Booking and CRM Customers book a free slot and pay a deposit at any hour. Every enquiry sits on one board. More → 03 Follow-up automation Missed-call text-back, quote chasers, reminders and review requests. Set up once, runs itself. More → 04 Meta ads Facebook and Instagram ads that land on a page built to book, with follow-up for anyone who does not. More → 05 Google ads Search ads and Local Services Ads, so you show up when someone nearby searches for what you do. More → How it fits One system Why one system rather than five suppliers? Because the gaps between them are where the jobs go missing. An ad that lands on a page that cannot book, a booking that never gets a reminder, a missed call nobody returns. Here the ad points at the website, the website books into the CRM, and the CRM sends the texts, so nothing falls between two suppliers. You can start with one piece and add the rest. Most owners start with the website or the missed-call text-back, because that is where the most work is leaking. The process Teardown, quote, build, handover How does a build work? The teardown. Ten minutes on your website, your Google listing and what happens when someone tries to reach you. Three things back: what is leaking, what to fix first, what it is worth in jobs. Free, by message. A flat quote. Every job is quoted flat and agreed before anything starts, with a date. No surprises, and no meeting that should have been a message. Built in public. A website takes days; a full system usually one to two weeks. You can watch it being made. Handover. Domain, code and accounts set up in your name. Walk away tomorrow and it all keeps working. The automations Missed-call text-back Anyone whose call you miss gets a text seconds later, with a link to book. How it works → Review requests Every customer gets asked for a Google review when the job is done, with one tap to leave it. How it works → Service reminders Customers get a text when they are due again: the boiler service, the MOT, the next cut. How it works → Quote chasing Quotes that go quiet get a friendly chaser, with a link to accept. How it works → Booking deposits A deposit taken at booking holds the slot and comes off the bill. How it works → On-my-way texts One tap tells the customer you have set off, when you will arrive and who is coming. How it works → By trade Your kind of business What does a website for your trade need? It depends on how your work comes in. A locksmith lives on the emergency call, a salon on the rebooking, a roofer on the quote. Find your trade to see what its website needs and the demos set up for it. Straight answers The questions people ask Questions people ask Skales What does Skales do? Skales builds websites, online booking and follow-up automation for UK service businesses, and runs Meta and Google ads that send people to them. The aim is one system that turns a search, a tap or a missed call into a booked job. Who is Skales for? Trades and local service businesses whose work comes in by phone, message or search: plumbers and heating engineers, electricians, roofers, builders, cleaners, garages, salons, clinics, and anyone else who books work with customers. Who will I actually deal with? Tom Griffiths. Skales is one person, so the person you message is the person who builds it. How much does it cost? Every job is quoted flat after a short call, and agreed before anything starts. The price depends on how many pages you need, whether you take bookings or deposits, which automations you want and whether you want ads. There are no prices on this site. How long does it take? A website on its own takes days. A full system with booking and follow-up usually takes one to two weeks, built in public so you can watch it being made. Do I own what you build? Yes. The domain, the code and the accounts are set up in your name from day one. Nothing is rented back to you monthly, and if you stopped working with me, everything would keep working. ### Missed-call text-back (https://skales.studio/automations/missed-call-text-back/)

Missed call text back for UK businesses | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Automations / Missed-call text-back Missed-call text-back : every missed call gets a reply. Missed-call text-back sends a text to anyone whose call you could not answer, seconds after it rings out, with a link to book or a quick question. It turns a missed call into a conversation before they ring the next business on Google. Read more Book a call Try the demo Inbox and missed calls The system, set up for six made-up businesses Running live Use it → Why it matters Missed-call text-back Why does it matter? When you are up a ladder or under a sink, you cannot answer. Plenty of people who reach voicemail do not leave a message; they ring the next number instead. A text back in the first minute keeps them talking to you. Your numbers What missed calls cost What are missed calls costing you? Calls you miss in a week 5 What a typical job is worth £250 Of those callers, how many would have booked? 1 in 4 1 in 3 1 in 2 £1,400 a month goes to whoever answers next. That is £16,800 a year. Book a call about it The calculator needs JavaScript. The sum is simple: missed calls a week × 4.3 weeks × the share who would have booked × what a job is worth. How it works Step by step How does missed-call text-back work? The call rings out. You are on a job and cannot pick up. The call goes unanswered, as it would now. The text goes out. Seconds later, the caller gets a text from your business: sorry you missed them, here is a link to book, or reply and you will ring back. They book or reply. They pick a slot on your booking page, or reply with what they need. Either way they have stopped looking elsewhere. You see it all. The missed call, the text and what happened next sit on one card in your CRM, so you know who to ring and who has already booked. The message What the customer gets What does the text say? Sorry I missed your call, I’m on a job. You can book a time here: larchfield.co.uk/book, or reply with what you need and I’ll ring you back. Larchfield Heating An example for Larchfield Heating, a made-up business. Yours is written with you, in your words. What it needs From you What does it need from me? A business number that can forward unanswered calls. Most UK mobile and landline networks can. Your booking link, if you take bookings. If not, the text asks what they need. The numbers you do not want texted, such as suppliers and family. See it run Live demos with a made-up business. You play the customer, then see what the business sees. About a minute each. About a minute · works on your phone Missed call, booked Call your own business, let it ring out, and watch the text turn into a booking with a deposit. A review request goes to the customer by text when the job is marked done, with one tap straight to your Google review box. Asking every customer at the right moment is how a small business builds its rating without chasing anyone. Read more Book a call Try the demo Google reviews The system, set up for six made-up businesses Running live Use it → Why it matters Review requests Why does it matter? Happy customers mean to leave a review and forget. The ones who remember unprompted are often the unhappy ones. Asking everyone, the same day, while they are still pleased with the work, changes who writes your reviews. Read more How it works Step by step How does review requests work? The job is marked done. You move the job to Done in the CRM, or the invoice is paid. The request goes out. A couple of hours later, the customer gets a short text thanking them and asking for a review, with a link that opens your Google review box. One tap to review. They tap, pick the stars and write a line. No searching for your business, no signing in to anything new. You reply. New reviews show up for you to reply to, so every review gets a response in your name. The message What the customer gets What does the text say? Thanks again for having us round today, Priya. Google does not allow filtering out unhappy customers before asking for a review, so everyone gets asked. A business that does good work comes out of that well. When is the best time to ask? The same day, a couple of hours after the job, while the work is fresh and they are still pleased. The timing can be changed for your trade. Does it work for repeat customers? Yes. Service reminders text your customers when they are due again: the annual boiler service, the MOT, the next haircut, the gutter clean. The work that comes round every year gets booked without anyone having to remember to ring. Read more Book a call Try the demo Reminders that rebook The system, set up for six made-up businesses Running live Use it → Why it matters Service reminders Why does it matter? Repeat work is the cheapest work you will ever win, and it is the easiest to lose. Customers do not forget you; they forget the date. Whoever reminds them first gets the job. Read more How it works Step by step How does service reminders work? The job sets the date. When a job that comes round is done (a service, an MOT, a cut), the next due date is worked out and saved with the customer. The reminder goes out. A few weeks before they are due, the customer gets a text saying so, with a link to book. A nudge if needed. If they do not book, one follow-up goes out closer to the date. Then it stops. The diary fills. Bookings from reminders land in your diary like any other, marked as returning customers. The message What the customer gets What does the text say? Quote chasing sends a friendly follow-up when a quote has not been accepted, a couple of days after it went out, with a link to accept or ask a question. Quotes that go quiet get a nudge without you having to remember who you priced up last Tuesday. Read more Book a call Try the demo Inbox and missed calls The system, set up for six made-up businesses Running live Use it → Why it matters Quote chasing Why does it matter? Pricing a job takes time, and most quotes are never chased because the person who wrote them is on another job. A customer who has gone quiet is often just busy. The one who follows up politely is the one they book. Read more How it works Step by step How does quote chasing work? The quote goes out. You price the job and send it from the CRM. The customer gets a link to see it and accept it. The system watches. It knows whether they have opened it, and whether they have accepted. The chaser goes out. If the quote is still open after a couple of days, the customer gets a short, friendly follow-up with the link again. Accepted becomes booked. When they accept, the job moves to Booked and the confirmation goes out. If they say no, it is closed and you know. The message What the customer gets What does the text say? Online booking deposits for service businesses | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Automations / Booking deposits Booking deposits: a booked slot that turns into a job. A booking deposit is a small payment the customer makes when they book online, which holds the slot and comes off the final bill. It turns a booking into a commitment, so the time you set aside is paid for. Book a call Try the demo Booking and the diary The system, set up for six made-up businesses Running live Use it → Why it matters Booking deposits Why does it matter? A no-show costs you the job and the job you turned away to fit them in. A deposit is the simplest fix: a booking with money behind it is a booking people keep, and the ones who cannot make it let you know. Read more How it works Step by step How does booking deposits work? They pick a slot. The customer chooses the job and a free time on your booking page. They pay the deposit. They pay by card on the same page. You choose which jobs take a deposit and how much. The slot is theirs. They get a confirmation with the deposit shown, and a reminder before the day. It comes off the bill. The deposit is taken off the final invoice. Your cancellation rules decide what happens if they cancel late. The message What the customer gets What does the text say? You’re booked: boiler service, Thursday 8 October at 8:00. Your deposit is paid and comes off the final bill. We’ll remind you the day before. A small deposit on the booking page is normal for salons, clinics, restaurants and more and more trades. Customers who are serious about the job pay it; the ones who were never going to turn up tend not to book. Where does the money go? Straight to your own payment account, set up in your name. An on-my-way text tells the customer you have set off, with a rough arrival time and who is coming, so they are in, the dog is shut away and the car is off the drive. Book a call Try the demo Booking and the diary The system, set up for six made-up businesses Running live Use it → Why it matters On-my-way texts Why does it matter? A wasted trip to an empty house costs a morning. A customer who is not sure when you are coming rings to ask, and calls you while you are driving. One text before you set off fixes both. How it works Step by step How does on-my-way texts work? You set off. On the way to the job, you tap On my way on the job sheet on your phone. The text goes out. The customer gets a text with who is coming and a rough arrival time. They get ready. They are in, the parking is clear, and they are not ringing you to ask where you are. Running late is one tap too. If a job overruns, one tap tells the next customer, so nobody is left waiting without knowing why. The message What the customer gets What does the text say? ### Skales vs a page builder (https://skales.studio/compare/page-builders/)

Web designer or Wix? Skales vs page builders | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Compare / Page builders Skales or a page builder like Wix or Squarespace? A page builder is the right choice if you enjoy building, have the evenings to do it, and want a site online for a small monthly fee. A hand-built Skales site is the better choice when the website’s job is to bring in work: it is faster, it books and follows up on its own, and you own it outright. Read more Side by side What A page builder Skales Who builds it You, from a template Me, by hand, for your business How you pay A subscription for as long as the site is live A flat quote for the build, agreed first. The business is very new and you just need something online. The site is a brochure and the work does not come in through it. When Skales is the better choice Your work comes in by phone and the site should turn visits into bookings. You want missed calls, quotes and reminders followed up without you. You would rather own the site than rent it. Straight answers The questions people ask Questions people ask Is a page builder cheaper? At the start, usually. Over a few years the subscription and the add-ons add up, and you still do not own the site. Which works out better depends on how long you keep it and what it brings in. Can you move my Wix or Squarespace site? Yes. The content comes across, every old address is redirected to its new page, and the new site replaces the subscription. More in every question, answered . ### Skales vs a Google Business Profile alone (https://skales.studio/compare/google-business-profile/)

Do I need a website with a Google Business Profile? | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Compare / Google Business Profile Do you need a website if you have a Google Business Profile? A Google Business Profile is free, and every local service business should have one, because it is what Google shows on the map and in local results. On its own it can be enough for a business that lives on calls from people nearby, but a website adds what the profile cannot: a page for each service and area, online booking and deposits, and a place that is yours rather than Google’s. Read more Side by side What A Google Business Profile alone Skales Where it shows Google Maps and the local results for searches near you Search results for each service and area you cover, and AI assistants that read web pages Who controls it Google’s layout and rules, and anyone can suggest an edit You: every word, page and photo, with the domain and accounts in your name Room to explain A short description, a list of services, photos and posts A page for each service, answering the questions customers ask before they ring Bookings Calls, messages, and a link to a booking page if you have one Booking, deposits and reminders on your own site Reviews Where your Google reviews live Shows them off, and review requests send every new customer to leave one When a Google Business Profile alone is the better choice Nearly all your work is calls from people nearby who find you on the map. You offer one or two services and there is little to explain. You are just starting and want to be findable today at no cost. When Skales is the better choice You offer several services, or cover several towns, and want to be found for each. You want customers to book and pay a deposit without ringing you. You run ads, or plan to, and need a page that turns the click into a booking. Straight answers The questions people ask Questions people ask Is a Google Business Profile enough for a tradesperson? For some, yes, especially when the work is local and arrives by phone. Once you want to be found for each service and area, take bookings online or run ads, you need pages of your own for the profile and the ads to point to. Does a website help my Google Business Profile? Yes. The profile links to your website, and a site whose business name, area and phone number match the profile, with a page for each service, gives Google more to go on when it decides which businesses to show. Can I have a Google Business Profile without a shop? Yes. Google lets businesses that visit their customers set a service area and hide their address, so a sole trader working from home can still appear in local results for the areas they cover. But it runs on Meta’s platform and rules, it is not built to be found by people searching Google for your service, and every enquiry becomes a conversation in messages, so most businesses that need new customers end up wanting both. ### Every question, answered (https://skales.studio/faq/)

Questions about websites, booking and ads | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / FAQ Every question, answered. Short, straight answers about what Skales builds, what it costs, how long it takes and who owns it, then the questions for each service, automation and comparison. If yours is not here, ask it on a call. The basics Websites Booking and CRM Follow-up automation Meta ads Google ads Missed-call text-back Review requests Service reminders Quote chasing Booking deposits On-my-way texts Skales vs a page builder Skales vs a monthly trade website Skales vs a missed-call app Skales vs a directory listing Skales vs a Google Business Profile alone Skales vs a Facebook page The basics Start here The basics What does Skales do? Skales builds websites, online booking and follow-up automation for UK service businesses, and runs Meta and Google ads that send people to them. The aim is one system that turns a search, a tap or a missed call into a booked job. Who is Skales for? Trades and local service businesses whose work comes in by phone, message or search: plumbers and heating engineers, electricians, roofers, builders, cleaners, garages, salons, clinics, and anyone else who books work with customers. Who will I actually deal with? Tom Griffiths. Skales is one person, so the person you message is the person who builds it. How much does it cost? Every job is quoted flat after a short call, and agreed before anything starts. The price depends on how many pages you need, whether you take bookings or deposits, which automations you want and whether you want ads. There are no prices on this site. How long does it take? A website on its own takes days. A full system with booking and follow-up usually takes one to two weeks, built in public so you can watch it being made. Do I own what you build? Yes. The domain, the code and the accounts are set up in your name from day one. Nothing is rented back to you monthly, and if you stopped working with me, everything would keep working. Can you guarantee I will rank first on Google? No, and nobody honest can. What a well-built site does is give you the best chance: pages written for what your customers search, proper structured data, a fast site and a consistent Google Business Profile. Searches for your trade in your area are the ones to win first. Are the businesses on this site real? No. Every business, person, review and phone number in the demos and builds on this site is invented, and each one is labelled. They show how the systems work; no client is named or shown. Can I try it before I talk to anyone? Yes. The live demos on the Try it page run in your browser: call a business, book a job, or move a lead across a CRM board, then see what the business sees. Websites The full page Websites How long does a website take? A website on its own takes days. A full system with booking and follow-up usually takes one to two weeks, and you can watch it being built. How much does a website cost? Every job is quoted flat after a short call, because the price depends on how many pages you need, whether you take bookings or deposits, and which automations you want. There are no prices on this site and no monthly fee for a page builder. Do I own the website? Yes. The domain, the code and the accounts are set up in your name from day one. If you stopped working with me tomorrow, the site would keep working. I already have a website. Will I lose my Google ranking if it is rebuilt? Not if it is done properly. Every old address is redirected to its new page, so the links Google already knows keep working, and the new pages are faster and better structured than the old ones. Booking and CRM The full page Booking and CRM Can customers book at night or at weekends? Yes, that is the point. The booking page shows your free slots at any hour, so a customer who finds you at 10pm books then, instead of meaning to ring you in the morning. Can two people book the same slot? No. A slot disappears the moment it is taken, on every device. Do my customers need to download an app? No. Booking, paying the deposit and every text they get works in the browser on their phone. I quote rather than book. Is this still for me? Yes. The CRM board works the same way for quotes: every enquiry gets a reply, every quote gets chased if it goes quiet, and accepted quotes become booked jobs. Can I see where my enquiries come from? Yes. Every enquiry is tagged with where it came from (your website, Google, a missed call, an ad), so you can see which ones turn into booked work. Follow-up automation The full page Follow-up automation What does it cost to run? The setup is quoted flat, like everything else. After that, the only running cost is the texts themselves, billed by the text provider. Can I change what the messages say? Yes. Every message is written with you before it goes live, and any of them can be changed or paused with a message to me. Will it text my suppliers or family when I miss their calls? Not if you do not want it to. Numbers you know can be left out, so only new callers get the text. Do I need the website and CRM as well? No, but they work best together. Missed-call text-back runs on its own, and review requests only need a way to mark a job done, which can be an invoice being paid. Quote chasing and reminders need somewhere to keep the jobs, which is what the CRM is for. Meta ads The full page Meta ads How much should I spend on ads? It depends on your area, your trade and how many jobs you can take on. We agree a test budget on the call, the spend goes to Meta from your own account, and you can change it at any time. Can you guarantee leads? No, and nobody honest can. What you do get is a clear view of what the ads cost and what they booked, so you can decide whether to keep going. Do I need a website first? The ads need a page built to book. If you do not have one, I build it as part of the job, and it carries on working for you whether the ads are running or not. Facebook or Instagram? Both run from one Meta account. Where the budget goes depends on where your customers are, and the tracking shows which one books. Who owns the ad account? You do. It is set up in your name like everything else, so if you stop working with me, the account, the audience data and the history stay with you. Google ads The full page Google ads How much should I spend on Google Ads? It depends on how competitive your trade is in your area and how many jobs you want. We agree a test budget on the call, the spend goes to Google from your own account, and you can change it at any time. How quickly do Google Ads work? Search ads can start showing as soon as Google approves them, so they are the fastest way to appear for searches you are not ranking for yet. Getting the cost per job down takes a few weeks of tuning. Should I do ads or SEO? Usually both. Ads bring enquiries while the website earns its place in the normal results, which takes months. Once the site ranks for a search, you can spend less on ads for it. Can you guarantee the top spot? No. Where an ad appears depends on the budget, the competition and Google. What you get is a clear view of what each booked job cost. Who owns the Google Ads account? You do. It is set up in your name, so the account, the data and the history stay with you. Missed-call text-back The full page Missed-call text-back Does it work with my mobile number? Yes. Your phone forwards calls you do not answer, and the text goes out from there. You keep your number and answer calls exactly as you do now. Will it text suppliers, family or spam callers? Numbers you know can be left out, so only new callers get the text. How fast does the text go? Within seconds of the call ringing out, while the caller still has their phone in their hand. Will it spam my customers? No. It only texts people who have just rung you, once, about the call they made. Nobody is added to a marketing list. Review requests The full page Review requests Can it only ask the happy customers? No, and it should not. Google does not allow filtering out unhappy customers before asking for a review, so everyone gets asked. A business that does good work comes out of that well. When is the best time to ask? The same day, a couple of hours after the job, while the work is fresh and they are still pleased. The timing can be changed for your trade. Does it work for repeat customers? Yes. It can ask once and then leave them alone, so a regular is not asked after every visit. Can I show my reviews on my website? Yes. Real reviews can appear on your site, and once there are enough, in your search results too. Nothing is ever made up. Service reminders The full page Service reminders Which businesses is this for? Any business where the work comes round: boiler services and landlord certificates, MOTs and car services, hair and beauty appointments, window and gutter cleaning, check-ups and maintenance contracts. Can it use my existing customer list? Yes. A spreadsheet with names, numbers and the date of their last job is enough to start. How many reminders does a customer get? Usually one, and one follow-up if they do not book. Then it stops until next time. Is it allowed to text past customers? A reminder about a service they have had before, from a business they used, is the kind of message most customers expect. Anyone who replies to opt out is never texted again. Quote chasing The full page Quote chasing Will customers find it pushy? Not one polite message a couple of days later. It reads like a business that cares about the job, and customers often reply to say they had simply not got round to it. How many times does it chase? Once by default, with a second follow-up if you want one. After that the quote is left alone. What if the customer has already accepted? Then no chaser goes. It only follows up quotes that are still open. Can I still send my own quotes? Yes. You price the job; the system sends it and follows it up. Booking deposits The full page Booking deposits Will a deposit put customers off? A small deposit on the booking page is normal for salons, clinics, restaurants and more and more trades. Customers who are serious about the job pay it; the ones who were never going to turn up tend not to book. Where does the money go? Straight to your own payment account, set up in your name. What if a customer cancels? Your rules decide. Many businesses refund with enough notice and keep the deposit for late cancellations, and the booking page says so before they pay. Can some jobs be booked without a deposit? Yes. You choose which jobs take one, so a free quote visit can be booked without paying anything. On-my-way texts The full page On-my-way texts Does it track my location? No. It sends the text when you tap the button, with the arrival time you choose. Nobody is followed on a map. Can my team use it? Yes. Each person taps from their own job sheet, and the text says who is coming. What about the night before? Every booking already gets a reminder the day before. The on-my-way text is for the morning of the job. Is this only for trades? No. It suits anyone who goes to the customer: cleaners, mobile hairdressers, dog groomers, mechanics, surveyors. Skales vs a page builder The full page Skales vs a page builder Is a page builder cheaper? At the start, usually. Over a few years the subscription and the add-ons add up, and you still do not own the site. Which works out better depends on how long you keep it and what it brings in. Can you move my Wix or Squarespace site? Yes. The content comes across, every old address is redirected to its new page, and the new site replaces the subscription. Skales vs a monthly trade website The full page Skales vs a monthly trade website Why not just pay monthly? If the site is a business card, a monthly plan is fine. If it is meant to bring in work, it needs pages written for your searches, booking and follow-up, and it is better owned than rented. Can I keep my domain if I move? Usually, yes. If the domain is in your name, it moves with you. If the provider registered it in theirs, ask them to transfer it to you first. How do customers choose a heating engineer? Nobody shops around for a boiler repair on a cold evening. They search on their phone, ring the first number that looks local and Gas Safe, and if it rings out they ring the next one. Servicing is the opposite: steady yearly work that drifts away because nobody reminds the customer, while new boiler quotes go quiet as the customer waits on two more. Should my Gas Safe number be on my website? Yes, on every page, with a link to the Gas Safe Register so a customer can check it in seconds. It is one of the first things people look for before they let someone work on their boiler. Can it remind landlords when their gas safety certificate is due? Yes. The date of each check is saved against the property, and the landlord gets a text before the next one is due with a link to book. A landlord with several properties has a date for each. I’m booked up already. Why would I want online booking? Because it lets you decide what goes in the diary. Services are booked online into the slots you open, while breakdowns still come to you by phone, so the planned work stops interrupting the urgent work. It should turn the bigger enquiries into quotes that get followed up, and bring landlords back when their next electrical report is due. Quote chasing A rewire or a board change is often priced against other firms, and the electrician who follows up is still in the running when the customer decides. How it works → Service reminders Landlord EICRs come round again, and the reminder goes to the landlord or the agent before the report runs out, not after. How it works → On-my-way texts Customers need to be in, with the freezer and the home office ready for the power going off, so one tap telling them when you will arrive saves a wasted morning. How it works → Try it as an electrician: The CRM board → Missed call, booked → Questions Electricians: questions people ask More in every question, answered . How do customers choose an electrician? Electrical work arrives two ways. Small faults come by phone from people who want someone this week, and they go with whoever answers and looks properly registered. Rewires, consumer units and EV chargers are researched first and priced against other firms, so those quotes go quiet unless someone follows them up, and landlord EICRs come round again and are easy to lose track of. Should my scheme logo go on my website? Yes, with a link to where customers can check your registration. A logo on its own can be copied by anyone; a link to the register is proof. Can letting agents send me lots of EICRs at once? Yes. The landlord page takes several addresses in one enquiry, each property lands on the CRM board, and when each report is done its next due date is saved so the reminder goes out on its own. Do I need a separate page for EV charger installs? Yes. People search for the job rather than for an electrician, so a page that explains the survey, the install and what you need from them is the one that gets found. The same goes for consumer units and EICRs. It also needs a fast way to report a leak and a quote process that follows up, because re-roofs are compared and a storm brings every call at once. How it works → Quote chasing A re-roof is a big decision, and a follow-up a couple of days after the quote is the moment to answer the questions the customer has not asked yet. Roofing customers cannot see the problem and have usually been warned about doorstep roofers, so they look hard at who they ring. After a storm the phone goes all day, and calls missed on the scaffold are calls lost. A re-roof is a big decision priced against other firms, and the quote that comes with photos, a clear explanation and a follow-up is the one that stays in the running. How do I show customers I’m not a cowboy? Real photos of your own roofs, a business address, your guarantee in writing and reviews from real local customers. Stock photos of perfect roofs do the opposite. Should my website give prices? It can give a range, if you want it to. How it works → Try it as a builder: The CRM board → Questions Builders and joiners: questions people ask More in every question, answered . How do customers choose a builder? Building work mostly starts with a recommendation, and the first thing that person does is look you up. My work comes from word of mouth. Do I need a website? The person you were recommended to will still look you up before they ring. Say plainly on the site what you take on and where, and ask the right questions on the form. You can then see at a glance which enquiries fit before you ring anyone back. Can I send quotes from the system? Yes. You price the job and send it from the CRM, and the customer gets a link to read and accept it. Book a call Try it as a locksmith Larchfield Heating · Inbox and missed calls Live Inbox and missed calls , set up for Larchfield Heating, a made-up plumbing and heating firm. Full screen → What it needs What should a website for locksmiths do? A locksmith’s website has to prove two things fast to someone standing outside a locked door: that you are a real local locksmith rather than a call centre, and that they can reach you now. That means your name, face, van and area on the page, a call button that never leaves the screen, and a text back to any call you miss. Read more 01 A call button fixed to the bottom of the screen on a phone, for the customer on the doorstep. 02 Your name, a photo of you and the van, and the area you cover, so customers know who is coming. 03 How you open doors without damage where you can, and that the price is agreed before you start. 04 Insurance-approved locks explained, such as BS 3621 mortice locks, for customers whose insurer asks for them. 05 Separate pages for lockouts, lock changes, uPVC door repairs, landlord changeovers and commercial work. Websites Built from scratch, like these. Each one is made for its trade and works like the real thing. The businesses are made up, so no client is on show. Kestrel Electrical Electrician Kerb & Camber Garage Overhead Drone survey & filming Then it runs itself The three automations that matter most. Missed-call text-back A locked-out caller does not wait long before trying the next number, and a text saying you have seen it and asking for the address keeps them waiting for you instead. How it works → On-my-way texts Someone stuck outside wants to know who is coming and roughly when, and a text with your name is reassuring when a stranger is about to open their door. How it works → Review requests People choosing a locksmith in a hurry lean on reviews, so asking every customer once the door is open builds the record that wins the next lockout. How it works → Try it as a locksmith: Missed call, booked → Questions Locksmiths: questions people ask More in every question, answered . How do customers choose a locksmith? Lockouts are searched for on a phone, on the doorstep, often in the dark, and the customer rings the first number that looks local. Many have heard of call centres that pass the job to whoever is free, so a real name, a real address and clear terms count for a lot. The rest of the work, lock changes after a burglary or a house move, upgrades for insurance and landlord changeovers, is planned and easily lost when the phone is the only way in. How do I show I’m local and not a call centre? Your own name, a photo of you and the van, a business address and the towns you cover, all on the page. Leave out stock photos and anything that reads like a national network. Is it worth a page for every town I cover? Only for places you genuinely cover, and only if each page says something real about working there. Thin copies of the same page with the town name swapped can do more harm than good with Google. Does the missed-call text work in the middle of the night? Yes, it goes out whatever the hour. What it says is up to you, so at night it can say when you can get there, or that you will ring back first thing. How do customers choose a chimney sweep? Reminders do most of it. How do customers choose a pest controller? Pest problems are urgent and a little embarrassing, so people search for the pest by name and ring the first local firm that seems to know what it is doing. Every message is written with you, so they can say who is coming and when without naming the pest or the problem. Can it keep track of commercial contract visits? Yes. How do customers choose a removals firm? Moving home is stressful and dates move, so customers ask for quotes early and decide late. How much should the quote form ask? Enough to price the move or decide it needs a survey: addresses, property sizes, access and the date. Anything more can wait for the survey, because a long form puts people off before they send it. How do customers choose a mobile mechanic? Customers ring a mobile mechanic when the car will not start, when they cannot get it to a garage, or because they would rather not lose a day waiting in one. They want to know quickly whether you cover their street and whether the job can be done where the car is. The calls come while you are under a car, and a job that went well is rarely followed by a reminder when the next service is due. Can customers book a mobile mechanic online? Yes. They enter the registration, choose the job or describe the fault, and give the address where the car will be. Only the slots you open are offered, and postcodes outside your area are turned away politely before they reach you. Can a mobile mechanic do an MOT? No. An MOT has to be carried out at an approved test centre. Many mobile mechanics collect the car, take it for its test and bring it back, and if you offer that, the website should say so. How do I stop people booking jobs I cannot do on a driveway? List the jobs you do on site and the ones that need a garage, and make the booking ask what the car needs. Anything outside the list arrives as an enquiry for you to look at, not as a booked slot. Booking deposits Treatment slots are long, and a deposit means a late cancellation does not cost you the afternoon. How it works → Try it as a beauty clinic: Book and pay a deposit → Questions Beauty and aesthetics clinics: questions people ask More in every question, answered . How do customers choose a beauty clinic? Clients research a treatment for a while before booking, reading about the practitioner, the products and what recovery looks like. Plenty of treatments start with a consultation, and the gap between consultation and treatment is where clients drift away. Courses and top-ups are predictable repeat work that depends on the client remembering, and no-shows on long appointments are the costliest gaps in the diary. Can you run Facebook ads for anti-wrinkle injections? Not for the injections themselves. Botulinum toxin is a prescription-only medicine, and UK advertising rules do not allow it to be promoted to the public, including on social media. Ads can promote a consultation with you instead, and the landing page keeps to the same rules. Should consultations be booked separately from treatments? Yes, for anything that needs one. New clients book a consultation first, and the treatment is booked once you have agreed it is right for them. Returning clients can book treatments directly. Can it remind clients when they are due a top-up ? Yes. When a treatment is done, the next due date is saved, and the client gets a text ahead of it with a link to book. If they do not book, one more goes out nearer the time, and that is all. People looking for a dentist want to know one thing first: whether you will take them on, and on what basis. Existing patients want to book check-ups and hygiene appointments without phoning the moment the line opens, and urgent cases want to know whether there is a same-day slot. Recalls are where work leaks: patients mean to book their next check-up, forget, and drift until something hurts. Should the website say if we are not taking NHS patients? Yes. It is the first thing people want to know, and saying it clearly spares your reception the same call all day. If you are taking private patients, say how to register. Can check-up recalls go by text? Yes. Each patient’s next check-up date is saved when they are seen, and a recall text goes out before it so they can pick a time online. Anyone who does not book gets one reminder closer to the date. Can patients book with a specific dentist or hygienist? Yes. They choose the appointment type and the clinician, then a free time. Taken slots disappear, so nobody is double booked. Is a missed-call text appropriate for a law firm? Yes, if the wording is right. How do customers choose an estate agent? Buyers and tenants find properties on the portals, but sellers and landlords choose an agent differently: they look at who sells in their street, read reviews and check the agent’s own website before booking valuations. Calls from buyers and tenants come in all day and ring out during viewings. Work leaks when a valuation is done and nobody follows up the decision, and when the agent heading to a valuation has no quick way to say they are running late. Do I need a website when everything is on the portals? Buyers find houses on the portals, but sellers and landlords choose an agent, and they check your website when they do. It is the page that wins instructions, so it is the one to build properly. What does a letting agent have to show on its website? In England, letting agents must publish their fees, the redress scheme they belong to and, if they hold client money, their client money protection scheme. I build those in from the start, and your own compliance checks have the final say. Can sellers book a valuation online? Yes. They choose a time and give the address and a few details about the property, and it lands in your diary and on the CRM board. The proposal you send afterwards is followed up if it goes quiet. How it works → Review requests Blinds and shutters are bought with the eyes. A review with a photo of the finished room is what the next customer looks at first. How do customers choose a blinds company? People look for blinds or shutters when they move, redecorate or tire of a window that faces the street. They browse photos for ideas, then book a home visit to see samples and be measured, often with two companies. After the visit comes a quote, and it can sit while they decide on fabric, colour or budget. Made-to-measure orders then take a few weeks before fitting, and customers want to know where their order is. Can customers book a blinds measuring visit online? Yes. They choose a time, say which rooms and products they are thinking about, and get a confirmation and a reminder the day before. How do I follow up quotes after a home visit? The quote is sent from the board, and a friendly follow-up goes a few days later if there is no answer. It stops the moment the customer accepts or replies. Can I take a deposit when a customer accepts a quote? Yes. The acceptance link can take a deposit by card, so the order can be placed the same day and the fitting booked once it arrives. Full screen → What it needs What should a website for vets do? A vet practice’s website needs opening hours, what to do in an emergency out of hours, the team and the services you offer, and a way for owners to book or request an appointment online. It should then remind owners when vaccinations, flea and worm treatments or check-ups are due, because routine care depends on owners remembering, and a phone line that is busy at opening time loses some of the ones who do. Read more 01 Opening hours, and clear out-of-hours emergency instructions at the top of every page. 02 Online booking or appointment requests for routine visits, with the pet’s name, species and the reason for the visit. 03 The team, vets and nurses, with their interests, and any RCVS Practice Standards accreditation you hold. 04 The services you offer, from vaccinations and neutering to dental work and nurse clinics, and whether you see exotic pets. 05 How to register a new pet, and what to bring to the first visit. Owners look for a vet when they get a puppy or kitten, move house or want a change from their old practice. They compare a few nearby, look at the team and the hours, and check what happens at night. Day to day, most contact is a phone call at opening time to book or ask a question, which is when the front desk is busiest. Routine care runs on a calendar of boosters, treatments and check-ups, and owners rely on a reminder to keep to it. Can pet owners book vet appointments online? Yes. They pick the pet, the reason and a time, or send a request for the team to confirm, and get a confirmation and a reminder before the visit. How do I remind owners when vaccinations are due? Where to call out of hours, at the top of every page and in the same words as your phone message, so a worried owner at night does not have to search for it. Full screen → What it needs What should a website for opticians do? An optician’s website needs eye tests bookable online, the services you offer, from NHS and private tests to contact lenses and specialist clinics, and photos of the practice and the frames you stock. It should then remind each patient when their next test is due and tell them when their glasses are ready, because most patients will not remember the date themselves, and the practice that reminds them is the one they come back to. Read more 01 Eye tests bookable online, with NHS and private options and times that include any evenings or Saturdays you open. 02 The services you offer: eye tests, contact lenses, children’s tests, dry eye or other clinics, and home visits if you do them. 03 Photos of the practice and the frame ranges you stock, so people know what to expect before they visit. 04 Your optometrists and dispensing opticians, with their GOC registration. 05 Who can have an NHS sight test, in plain words, and what to bring to the appointment. Service reminders Most patients will not remember when their next test is due. A recall sent at the right time, with a link to book, brings them back to you rather than the chain they walk past. How it works → Missed-call text-back When everyone in the practice is with a patient, a caller gets a text with a link to book a test online instead of trying again later. How it works → Review requests A review asked for once the new glasses are collected, while the patient is pleased with them, helps the next person choose an independent practice. How it works → Try it as an optician: Book and pay a deposit → Questions Opticians: questions people ask More in every question, answered . How do customers choose an optician? People look for an optician when their eyes change, their glasses break, or a reminder arrives from their last practice. Many choose between a high street chain and an independent nearby, and they look at the practice, the frames and whether they can book at a time that suits them. After the test comes choosing frames, a wait for the glasses and a trip to collect them. Then nothing happens until the next test is due, often a year or two later, unless something reminds them. Can patients book an eye test online? Yes. They choose NHS or private, the type of test and a time, and get a confirmation and a reminder the day before. How do recall reminders work for opticians? Each patient keeps the date their next test is due. A message goes when it is close, with a link to book, and another later if they have not booked. Can patients be told when their glasses are ready? Yes. When the order arrives, the patient gets a message saying it is ready to collect, with your opening hours, so glasses do not sit uncollected on the shelf. Full screen → What it needs What should a website for wedding venues do? A wedding venue’s website needs photos of each space through the seasons, the capacities and what is included, a way to ask about dates and online booking for show rounds. It should then answer every enquiry quickly, take a deposit to hold a date and keep the couple updated as the day gets closer, because couples enquire at several venues at once and tend to book the one that answered first and made the next step easy. Signal 2027 Festival Marée Fragrance house Atelier Voss Architecture practice Then it runs itself The three automations that matter most. Quote chasing Couples enquire at several venues at once. How it works → Booking deposits A deposit taken online holds the date the moment a couple decides, rather than waiting on a bank transfer while another couple asks about the same Saturday. How it works → Review requests Couples read what other couples say. A review asked for after the wedding, with a photo from the day, is what the next couple trusts. How it works → Try it as a wedding venue: Book and pay a deposit → The CRM board → Questions Wedding venues: questions people ask More in every question, answered . How do customers choose a wedding venue? Couples start looking soon after they get engaged, often a year or more before the date. They shortlist venues from photos, send enquiries to several at once, usually in the evening or at the weekend, and ask about dates, numbers and what is included. The next step is a show round, and after that a decision that can take weeks. Once they book, there are menus, numbers, suppliers and timings to settle, and a steady stream of messages in the months before the day. Can couples book a wedding venue show round online? Yes. They choose a time for a show round or an open day, give their rough date and numbers, and get a confirmation and a reminder before they visit. How do I stop losing couples who enquire at several venues? Reply fast and keep in touch. The enquiry gets an answer straight away with your brochure and a link to book a show round, and a friendly follow-up goes later if they go quiet. Can a deposit be taken online to hold a wedding date? Yes. When a couple decides, they pay the deposit by card from a link, and the date shows as held in your diary at that moment. ### What a missed call actually costs a service business (https://skales.studio/notes/what-a-missed-call-costs/)

What a missed call actually costs a service business Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Notes 3 September 2026 · Tom Griffiths What a missed call actually costs a service business The sum behind the missed-call text-back, with every assumption on the table, and why the number survives a sceptic. A missed call costs a service business more than the job on the other end of it, because the customer who rang is usually ringing the next firm on the list within the hour. The calculator on the missed-call text-back page meters that leak from three numbers you already know: how many calls a week ring out, what an average job is worth, and how many of those callers would have booked. Why the model asks how many would have booked Most missed-call calculators quietly assume every missed caller would have booked. They would not. Some ring back, some were price-checking, some booked elsewhere before you saw the voicemail. The calculator makes that share an explicit choice, one in four, one in three or one in two, and prints the working under the figure, so the headline is a number a sceptical owner can check, not a marketing number. What a text-back in under a minute changes A missed-call text-back sends the customer a message seconds after the ring-out, asks one question, and turns a voicemail into a conversation. The customer who was about to dial the next number replies instead. The follow-up automation on this site does exactly that, and the missed-call demo on the Try page shows the sequence end to end. Open the calculator, put your own numbers in, and argue with it. That is what it is for. Open the calculator Book a call s k ales Websites & systems for service businesses. One person, United Kingdom. Twelve websites and one system running live on this site, every business in them invented. ### Privacy notice (https://skales.studio/privacy/)

Privacy notice: your data and who sees it | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Privacy notice Privacy notice Skales Studio is Tom Griffiths, one person in the United Kingdom. This page says what personal information the site and the studio collect, why, who else sees it, how long it is kept, and how to have it changed or deleted. Who is responsible for your information? Tom Griffiths, trading as Skales Studio, in the United Kingdom. For anything on this page, email thomasrgriffiths08@gmail.com , or message on WhatsApp. What is collected, and why? The three questions on /start. Your answers stay in your browser until you book a call; then they go into the booking with where you arrived from, so I can prepare. Booking a call. The booking page asks for your name, business, town, phone, email and what you would like help with. They go to Calendly, which runs the booking calendar, and I use them to prepare for the call. The free teardown. Your name, number and a line about your business, sent from your own WhatsApp or email. Messages. Whatever you send me by email, WhatsApp or Instagram, so I can reply. The live demos. Anything you type into the demos on /try/ stays in your browser and is not sent anywhere. Visiting the site. The site is hosted on Cloudflare Pages, run by Cloudflare, which keeps standard server logs (IP address, browser and the pages requested) to keep it running and secure. The fonts load from Google Fonts, so Google receives your IP address when a page loads. Ads and analytics. None at the moment: the site runs no analytics or advertising tags. If that changes, a cookie banner will ask you first and this page will say so. Clients. If we work together: your contact and business details, the accounts and content the build needs, and invoices. On what basis? Replying to an enquiry you started and preparing a quote: steps you asked for before a contract, and my legitimate interest in answering. Doing the work: the contract. Keeping invoices and records: the law. Server logs: my legitimate interest in keeping the site working and secure. Who else sees it? Nobody buys it, and it is never sold or swapped. The services that handle it for me are the site’s host (Cloudflare) and Calendly for bookings, plus email and WhatsApp when you choose to use them, and anyone the law requires me to share it with. Does it leave the UK? Some of those services are run by companies based in the United States, including Cloudflare, Google and Calendly. Where information goes outside the UK, it is covered by the safeguards UK data protection law requires, such as the UK–US data bridge or the contract clauses those companies use. How long is it kept? Enquiries that do not turn into work are deleted within 12 months of the last message. For clients, information is kept while we work together, and invoices and business records for as long as tax law requires. What can you ask for? You can ask to see what is held about you, have it corrected or deleted, restrict or object to how it is used, get a copy to take elsewhere. Email thomasrgriffiths08@gmail.com , or message on WhatsApp, and you will get an answer within one month. If you are unhappy with how your information has been handled, you can complain to the Information Commissioner’s Office at ico.org.uk or on 0303 123 1113. ### Cookies (https://skales.studio/cookies/)

Cookies: what this site stores and why | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Cookies Cookies This site sets no advertising or analytics cookies. The little it stores is there because you are using it, like your place in a demo, and it stays in your browser. What does the site store without asking? Only what makes the pages you are using work. It stays in your browser and is not sent anywhere unless you choose to send it. What Where How long Why Your answers on /start and your place in the demos Session storage Until you close the tab So the questions and the demos keep your answers as you move between screens. Where you arrived from, such as the Instagram link Session storage Until you close the tab So it can go with your booking, if you book a call. Are there ad or analytics cookies? No. The site runs no analytics or advertising tags at the moment. If that changes, a banner will ask you first, nothing will load unless you accept, and this page will list every cookie. What about the booking calendar? The booking page loads Calendly’s calendar so you can pick a time. Calendly sets its own cookies to make the booking work, under its own privacy policy. How do you change your choice? There is nothing to change at the moment. You can clear this site’s data in your browser settings at any time. The privacy notice covers everything else.
